articles.title: How international sourcing works, step by step
articles.summary: A plain guide to the stages of a sourcing requirement — from the first brief to delivery.
articles.author: Monoha Team
body: Sourcing from another market can look complicated from the outside. In practice it follows a clear sequence, and knowing that sequence makes every conversation with a supplier easier.
Write down what you need, the quantity, the quality standard and the date you need it by. A vague brief produces vague quotations.
Understand the market: who makes the product, typical lead times, and what questions to ask.
Compare suppliers on more than price — communication, reliability and the ability to meet your standard matter as much.
Agree specifications, samples and timelines in writing, and keep one clear channel of communication.
Check what arrives against the original requirement. That review is what makes the next order smoother.
